# SPEC-NNN: Specification Title

> Replace every placeholder before publication. This Specification must derive
> from accepted ADRs and may not introduce architecture.

## Summary

Summarize the implementation contract.

## Scope

Define exact behavior, modules, profiles, platforms, and integrations covered.

## Goals

- Contractual goal.

## Non-goals

- Explicit exclusion.

## Dependencies

List feature, module, platform, toolchain, and lifecycle prerequisites.

## Related ADRs

Explain how each accepted ADR governs this Specification. Do not merely repeat
the metadata list.

## Terminology

Define domain-specific terms used normatively.

## Public Contract

Define observable client behavior and compatibility guarantees.

## Module Contract

Define responsibilities, ownership, dependency direction, and internal
boundaries that implementation must preserve.

## Types / APIs

Specify signatures, visibility, semantics, invariants, and availability.

## Behavior

Define normal operation, ordering, inputs, outputs, and edge cases.

## State / Lifecycle

Define state, transitions, ownership, initialization, invalidation, teardown,
and illegal transitions.

## Capability Requirements

Define declared capabilities, behavior when absent, negotiation, and defaults.

## Backend Requirements

Define backend-independent behavior and backend/platform obligations.

## Error Handling

Define error domains, propagation, recovery, determinism, and fail-closed
behavior.

## Performance Requirements

Define measurable latency, throughput, memory, stack, allocation, binary-size,
or capacity requirements and measurement conditions.

## Compatibility

Define source, behavior, platform, data, and migration requirements.

## Testing Requirements

List required unit, conformance, integration, cross-profile, platform, and
hardware tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Measurable criterion with identifiable evidence.

## Implementation Notes

This section is non-authoritative guidance. It may suggest sequencing or known
techniques but cannot change the contracts above.

## Open Issues

List non-architectural issues that may remain during drafting. If an issue
requires a new architectural choice, pause Specification work and route it
through RFC/ADR review.

## References

- Accepted ADRs.
- Approved RFC and accepted Proposal.
- Architecture documents, legacy sources, code, tests, and evidence.
